questions.question: Which tribal nationalist from Jharkhand, known for fighting British exploitation and referred to as "Dharati Baba," led the Munda rebellion and is now commemorated in the Indian Parliament Museum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birsa Munda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Birsa Munda** was a charismatic tribal leader and folk hero from the **Munda tribe** who spearheaded a 19th-century religious and political movement in the **Chotanagpur Plateau** region (modern-day **Jharkhand**).
 
• He is revered by the tribal community as **Dharti Aba** or **Dharati Baba**, which translates to **Father of the Earth**, due to his struggle for tribal land rights and cultural identity.
 
• He led the **Munda Rebellion**, also known as **Ulgulan** (The Great Tumult), between **1899 and 1900** against the **British Raj** and the **Dikus** (outsiders/landlords) who exploited the tribal population.
 
• The movement specifically targeted the destruction of the traditional **Khuntkatti** land system by **Thikadars** and **Zamindars**, seeking to establish a **Munda Raj**.
 
• In recognition of his contribution to the Indian independence movement, his portrait was unveiled in the **Central Hall of the Indian Parliament** in **1989**, making him the only tribal leader to receive such an honor.
 
• The Government of India celebrates his birth anniversary, **November 15**, as **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluri Sitarama Raju**:

 
 
• A revolutionary from **Andhra Pradesh** who led the **Rampa Rebellion** (1922−24).
 
• He fought against the **1882 Madras Forest Act** and is famously called **Manyam Veerudu** (Hero of the Jungle).
 
 
 
• **Komaram Bheem**:
 
 
• A **Gond** tribal leader from **Telangana** who fought against the **Asaf Jahi dynasty** and the British.
 
• He is credited with the powerful slogan **Jal, Jangal, Jameen** (Water, Forest, Land).
 
 
 
• **Peer Ali Khan**:
 
 
• An Indian revolutionary and rebel who participated in the **Revolt of 1857** in **Patna, Bihar**.
 
• A bookbinder by profession, he was executed by the British for his role in the uprising.

questions.question: In May 2025, which renowned nuclear scientist of India passed away?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. M.R. Srinivasan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Muthanna Ramaswamy Srinivasan** (born 1930) was a legendary Indian nuclear scientist who served as the **Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission (AEC)** and **Secretary of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**.
 
• He is celebrated as the **architect of India's nuclear power program**, specifically for his pioneering work on the **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR)** technology, which utilized indigenous natural uranium and heavy water.
 
• He was the founding **Chairman and Managing Director** of the **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)**, an organization he helped establish in **1987** to streamline the commercial operation of nuclear power plants.
 
• Under his technical leadership, India successfully commissioned major nuclear projects including the **Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS)** at Kalpakkam and the **Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS)** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• His strategic vision helped India achieve **self-reliance** in the nuclear fuel cycle, including heavy water production and reactor design, during periods of severe international technology denial.
 
• He was a member of the **National Security Advisory Board** and played a vital role in representing India at the **International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)** in Vienna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Honors and Awards**:

 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan**: Conferred in **2015** for his exceptional contribution to science and engineering.
 
• **Padma Bhushan** (1990) and **Padma Shri** (1984): Awarded for his administrative and scientific excellence in nuclear development.
 
 
 
• **Notable Nuclear Figures**:
 
 
• **Dr. Homi Bhabha**: Known as the **Father of the Indian Nuclear Program**, he established the **Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)** and passed away in **1966**.
 
• **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**: Known as the **Missile Man of India**, he was a key figure in the **Pokhran-II** tests and served as the **11th President of India**; he passed away in **2015**.
 
• **Dr. Raja Ramanna**: A renowned physicist who directed the **Smiling Buddha (Pokhran-I)** test in **1974** and served as the **Director of BARC**; he passed away in **2004**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of involuntary action of humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vomiting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Involuntary actions** are physiological activities that occur automatically without any conscious thought or the will of the individual. These actions are primarily controlled by the **autonomous nervous system** and the **hindbrain**.
 
• **Vomiting** is a complex **reflex action** that involves the forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth. This action is coordinated by the **vomiting center** located in the **medulla oblongata** of the brain.
 
• The process of vomiting involves the simultaneous contraction of the **diaphragm** and **abdominal muscles**, coupled with the relaxation of the **cardiac sphincter**. Since these muscle movements are triggered by the brain without conscious intent, vomiting is an involuntary action.
 
• In contrast, activities such as **Writing**, **Talking**, and **Moving a chair** are categorized as **voluntary actions**. These are initiated by the **cerebrum** in the **forebrain** and require deliberate effort, decision-making, and conscious motor control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medulla Oblongata**:

 
 
• It is a vital part of the **hindbrain** that regulates several **autonomic functions** essential for survival.
 
• Besides vomiting, it controls **blood pressure**, **heartbeat**, **respiration**, and reflexes like **sneezing**, **swallowing**, and **coughing**.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Nervous System**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Somatic Nervous System**, it handles the movements of **skeletal muscles**.
 
• The **Cerebral Cortex** is responsible for processing the information required to perform complex tasks like **speech** and **fine motor skills** like writing.
 
 
 
• **Reflex Arc**:
 
 
• While vomiting is a reflex, some other involuntary responses occur via the **spinal cord** to allow for extremely rapid reactions to external stimuli, such as pulling a hand away from a **hot object**.

questions.question: What is TrailGuard AI installed at Similipal Tiger Reserve in February 2025?

options.text: An early warning system for flood like situation.
an AI enabled application for environmental approval for mega infrastructural projects.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A system with AI-enabled cameras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **TrailGuard AI** is a sophisticated **AI-powered surveillance system** designed specifically to enhance wildlife security and combat **illegal poaching** in protected areas.
 
• The technology was deployed in the **Similipal Tiger Reserve (STR)** in **Odisha** during **February 2025** to create a digital perimeter around the core tiger habitat.
 
• The system consists of **AI-enabled cameras** that utilize **edge computing** to process images instantly on the device rather than sending all raw footage to a central server.
 
• The primary function of these cameras is to detect **human intruders**, **poachers**, or **unauthorized vehicles** in real-time, filtering out images of wind-blown vegetation or non-target animals.
 
• Once a threat is identified, the system transmits **real-time alerts** and photographic evidence to **forest rangers** and **quick response teams** via satellite or cellular networks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Similipal Tiger Reserve**:

 
 
• Located in the **Mayurbhanj district** of **Odisha**, it is famous for being the only natural habitat in the world for **melanistic tigers** (black tigers).
 
• It was declared a **Tiger Reserve** in **1973** and became part of the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in **2009**.
 
• The reserve is home to a rich variety of flora and fauna, including the **Asian Elephant** and the **Chousingha**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Features**:
 
 
• The **TrailGuard AI** technology was developed by the conservation organization **Resolve** in partnership with **Intel** and **Hugging Face**.
 
• It employs the **Intel Movidius Vision Processing Unit (VPU)**, which allows the camera to operate for years on a small battery by using very low power.
 
• The device is compact and easily **camouflaged**, making it nearly invisible to intruders attempting to bypass traditional security measures.

questions.question: 'Khuded' folk songs are traditionally associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khuded** folk songs are deeply rooted in the cultural fabric of the **Garhwal region** of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• These songs primarily depict the **melancholy** and **suffering** of a married woman who is longing for her **maternal home** (referred to locally as **Maait**).
 
• The word **Khuded** originates from the local dialect word **Khuda**, which translates to the feeling of **homesickness** or the pain of separation from loved ones.
 
• Traditionally, these songs are performed by women while they are engaged in daily chores such as **gathering fodder** in the forests or working in the **agricultural fields** of the **Himalayan** slopes.
 
• The lyrics often describe the geographical barriers, such as high mountains and dense forests, that intensify the sense of isolation felt by the woman in her husband’s village.
 
• **Khuded** songs serve as a powerful medium for emotional release, reflecting the socio-cultural reality of historical **Garhwali** society where women were often married into distant villages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Folk Traditions of Uttarakhand**:

 
 
• **Chhopati**: These are popular **love songs** from the **Tehri Garhwal** district, typically sung in a **dialogue format** between men and women during cultural gatherings.
 
• **Bajuband**: A traditional folk song of the **shepherd community** in the **Garhwal** hills, often themed around themes of **love** and **sacrifice**.
 
• **Basanti**: These songs are composed to celebrate the arrival of the **spring season** and are usually sung individually or in groups during **Basant Panchami**.
 
• **Jhumelo**: A rhythmic dance-song performed during festivals, which highlights the **natural beauty** of the **Himalayas** and community bonding.
 
• **Jagars**: A unique form of **ritualistic vocal music** used to invoke local **deities** and spirits, common in both **Kumaon** and **Garhwal** regions.
 
 
 
• **Folk Music of Other States**:
 
 
• **Rajasthan**: Characterized by diverse styles like **Maand**, **Manganiyar**, and **Langa** traditions.
 
• **Assam**: Famous for **Bihu Geets** and the devotional **Borgeet** composed by **Srimanta Sankardev**.
 
• **Karnataka**: Known for **Bhavageete** (expressionist poetry) and the rhythmic **Dollu Kunitha**.

questions.question: 'Lemlawi', an instrument belonging to the Jew's harp family, is a traditional instrument of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lemlawi** is a traditional **Jew’s harp** (or mouth harp) that is deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of the **Mizo people** in **Mizoram**.
 
• It is categorized as a **lamellophone**, consisting of a flexible bamboo or metal tongue attached to a frame. The traditional version is usually carved from a single piece of **Sairil bamboo**.
 
• The instrument is played by placing it between the **teeth** or lips; the musician plucks the projecting tongue of the instrument with their finger while using their **mouth cavity** as a natural **resonator** to amplify the sound.
 
• Players can manipulate the **timbre** and pitch of the **Lemlawi** by changing the shape of their mouth and controlling their **breath**, creating a distinctive rhythmic and droning melody.
 
• Historically, the **Lemlawi** was used for personal relaxation and was a popular instrument for **young men and women** during **courtship** to communicate subtle feelings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mizoram**:

 
 
• **Khuang**: The most significant Mizo musical instrument, a **drum** made of hollowed wood and wrapped with **animal skin**, essential for all traditional dances.
 
• **Tuium**: A percussion instrument made of a **bamboo tube** with strings pulled out from the bamboo outer skin itself.
 
• **Seki**: A rhythmic instrument made from the **horns of a Mithun** (a local bovine), played by striking two horns together.
 
 
 
• **Telangana**:
 
 
• Features the **Oggu Dolu**, a hand-held drum used in **Oggu Katha** storytelling, and the **Kommulu**, a brass wind instrument.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Home to the **Jodia Pava** (double flute) and the **Ravanahatha**, an ancient bowed string instrument often used by folk musicians.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**:
 
 
• Known for the **Saraswati Veena** in classical music and folk instruments like the **Dollu** and **Tamate**.

questions.question: What does the evidence from the Indus Valley Civilization suggest about its people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They were excellent engineers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** (also known as the **Harappan Civilization**), existing roughly between **2500 BCE** and **1700 BCE**, provides extensive archaeological evidence of highly advanced **urban planning** and architectural mastery.
 
• Their cities, such as **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-daro**, were laid out on a meticulous **grid system** (gridiron pattern) where streets intersected at right angles, a feat that required sophisticated mathematical and **surveying skills**.
 
• The people developed a complex **drainage system** that was unparalleled in the ancient world; every house was connected to street drains made of **mortared brick** and covered with stone slabs or **terracotta** lids for easy maintenance.
 
• Structures like the **Great Bath** at Mohenjo-daro demonstrate their expertise in **civil engineering** through the use of **bitumen** (natural tar) for waterproofing, ensuring the massive tank remained leak-proof for centuries.
 
• The discovery of the **dockyard at Lothal** highlights their understanding of **hydrography** and **maritime engineering**, as it featured a lock system to regulate water flow during high and low tides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Standardization and Materials:**

 
 
• Harappans used **standardized burnt bricks** with a consistent ratio of **1:2:4** (thickness to width to length), which is a hallmark of an organized industrial society.
 
• In **Dholavira**, archaeologists found a sophisticated **water management system** consisting of giant **stone-cut reservoirs** and channels to harvest every drop of water in an arid environment.
 
• The **Citadel** or upper town was often built on raised platforms of **mud-bricks** to protect administrative buildings from frequent flooding of the **Indus River** and its tributaries.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the effect of deforestation on soil?

I. Physical properties of the soil get affected by plantation and vegetation.

II. Removal of the top layer of the soil exposes the lower, hard and rocky layers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plantation** and **vegetation** cover play a crucial role in maintaining the **physical properties** of the soil, such as its texture, structure, and **water-holding capacity**. Roots of trees and plants bind the soil particles together, preventing **soil erosion** and maintaining nutrient levels like **nitrogen** and **phosphorus**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Deforestation** leads to the exposure of the soil surface to agents of erosion like **wind** and **water**. When the fertile **topsoil** layer, which is rich in **humus**, is washed away, the lower, **hard and rocky layers** are revealed. These layers possess significantly less **organic matter** and are far less fertile than the surface soil. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deforestation**:

 
 
• It refers to the large-scale **clearing of forests** for agriculture, urbanization, or industrial purposes.
 
• It significantly disrupts the **water cycle** and increases **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** levels in the atmosphere, contributing to **global warming**.
 
 
 
• **Desertification**:
 
 
• The continuous removal of the topsoil layer through **erosion** gradually converts **fertile land** into **deserts**.
 
• This process reduces the **infiltration rate** of water into the ground, often leading to **floods** in nearby areas during heavy rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Soil Fertility**:
 
 
• The loss of **vegetative cover** prevents the replenishment of **nutrients** through the decomposition of leaves and organic matter, rendering the land unsuitable for **cultivation**.

questions.question: In the medals tally of the Commonwealth Games 2022, which of the following countries ranked below India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa**__.

• **Australia** secured the **1st rank** by winning a total of **178 medals** (67 Gold, 57 Silver, 54 Bronze). Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **England** finished in the **2nd rank** with a total of **176 medals** (57 Gold, 66 Silver, 53 Bronze). Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• **Canada** occupied the **3rd rank**, finishing just above India with **92 medals** (26 Gold, 32 Silver, 34 Bronze). Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• **South Africa** finished in the **9th rank** in the overall medals tally, securing only **27 medals** (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 11 Bronze). Since the 9th rank is numerically lower than India's 4th rank, it ranked below India. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

questions.question:
Poultry fowl suffer from several diseases caused by which of the following?

I. Virus

II. Bacteria
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poultry fowl** are highly susceptible to a variety of **viral infections** that can cause mass mortality and significant economic losses in the farming industry. Major viral diseases include **Ranikhet disease** (Newcastle Disease), **Fowl Pox**, and **Infectious Bursal Disease** (Gumboro). These viruses often target the respiratory, nervous, or immune systems of the birds. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Bacterial pathogens** are equally responsible for numerous poultry ailments that affect growth and egg-laying capacity. Common examples include **Fowl Cholera** (caused by Pasteurella multocida), **Salmonellosis**, and **Chronic Respiratory Disease** (caused by Mycoplasma). These infections typically spread through **contaminated feed**, water, or poor sanitation practices. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viral Disease Characteristics:**

 
 
• **Ranikhet Disease** is one of the most lethal viral diseases in India, characterized by **gasping**, nasal discharge, and **neurological symptoms** like paralysis.
 
• **Avian Influenza** (Bird Flu) is a highly contagious viral infection that can occasionally cross the species barrier to infect humans.
 
 
 
• **Bacterial Disease Characteristics:**
 
 
• **Fowl Cholera** usually presents as an acute **septicaemia** with high morbidity and sudden death in the flock.
 
• **Pullorum Disease**, caused by Salmonella pullorum, primarily affects young chicks and is transmitted through the **egg** from the mother bird.
 
 
 
• **Other Pathogens:**
 
 
• In addition to viruses and bacteria, poultry suffer from **fungal infections** like Aspergillosis (Brooder Pneumonia) and **parasitic diseases** such as Coccidiosis caused by protozoa.
 
• Prevention strategies involve **regular vaccination**, administration of **antibiotics** for bacterial issues, and maintaining strict **biosecurity** and hygiene in poultry sheds.

questions.question: The name of animal species _____ means "man of the forest" in the Malay language.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orangutan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Orangutan** is derived from the **Malay** and **Indonesian** words **orang**, which means **person** or **man**, and **hutan**, which means **forest**.
 
• When combined, the name literally translates to **man of the forest**, a reference to their high intelligence and predominantly **arboreal** lifestyle in dense tropical jungles.
 
• These **great apes** are geographically restricted to the rainforests of **Southeast Asia**, specifically inhabiting the islands of **Borneo** and **Sumatra**.
 
• They are recognized for their distinctive **reddish-brown hair** and extreme manual dexterity, sharing approximately **97 percent** of their DNA with humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orangutans (Genus Pongo)**:

 
 
• There are three distinct species: the **Bornean** (Pongo pygmaeus), the **Sumatran** (Pongo abelii), and the recently identified **Tapanuli** orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis).
 
• They are the largest tree-dwelling mammals and are known for their unique method of movement called **brachiation**.
 
 
 
• **Sumatran Tiger**:
 
 
• Scientifically known as **Panthera tigris sumatrae**, it is a critically endangered subspecies found only on the Indonesian island of **Sumatra**.
 
 
 
• **Komodo Dragon**:
 
 
• Recognized as **Varanus komodoensis**, it is the heaviest and largest lizard species on Earth, endemic to the **Lesser Sunda Islands** of Indonesia.
 
 
 
• **Irrawaddy Dolphins**:
 
 
• Known as **Orcaella brevirostris**, these are euryhaline dolphins found in coastal areas, estuaries, and rivers like the **Mekong** and the **Irrawaddy** in **South and Southeast Asia**.

questions.question: Which of the following bee is known as little bee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apis florae**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apis florae**, commonly referred to as the **Little Bee** or **Dwarf Honey Bee**, is the smallest species among the genus **Apis** in terms of body size.
 
• These bees are native to **South and Southeast Asia**, including countries like **India**, and are typically found in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• They build a **single vertical comb** that is usually no larger than the size of a human palm, often suspended from **twigs**, **bushes**, or **shrubbery** in open-air environments.
 
• Due to their small size and specific nesting habits, they produce a relatively small amount of honey, generally ranging from **200 to 900 grams** per colony annually.
 
• The **Apis florae** is known for being **docile** and less aggressive compared to larger species, although they exhibit a high tendency for **absconding** (leaving the nest) if disturbed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apis dorsata**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Rock Bee** or **Giant Honey Bee**.
 
• It is the **largest honeybee** species and is highly aggressive, making it difficult to domesticate.
 
• A single colony can yield **35 to 40 kg** of honey.
 
 
 
• **Apis cerana indica**:
 
 
• Popularly known as the **Indian Honey Bee** or **Eastern Honey Bee**.
 
• It is a **medium-sized** bee that is widely used for **apiculture** in India because it is relatively easy to domesticate in **moveable frames**.
 
• The average honey yield is approximately **2 to 5 kg** per colony.
 
 
 
• **Apis mellifera**:
 
 
• Known as the **European Honey Bee** or **Western Honey Bee**.
 
• It was introduced to India for **commercial beekeeping** due to its high honey production capacity and low swarming tendency.
 
• It can yield between **25 to 40 kg** of honey per colony.

questions.question:
In living organisms, nitrogen is a component of which of the following?

I. Proteins II. Chlorophyll
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is an indispensable constituent of **proteins**, which are complex **macromolecules** formed by long chains of **amino acids**. Every amino acid contains a central carbon atom bonded to an **amino group** (-NH₂), a carboxyl group, and a side chain; the presence of **nitrogen** in the amino group makes it a fundamental building block for all cellular structures, **enzymes**, and **hormones**. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• **Chlorophyll**, the green pigment located in the **chloroplasts** of plants, algae, and **cyanobacteria**, is essential for **photosynthesis**. The molecular structure of chlorophyll (such as **Chlorophyll a**, C₅₅H₇₂O₅N₄Mg) contains a **porphyrin ring** composed of four **pyrrole** rings, each of which contains a **nitrogen** atom coordinated to a central **magnesium** atom. Hence, statement II is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen** is a major **macronutrient** required by plants in the greatest amount, typically absorbed from the soil as **nitrate** (NO₃−) or **ammonium** (NH₄⁺).

 
 
• **Nucleic Acids**: Nitrogen is a key component of **DNA** and **RNA**, forming the **nitrogenous bases** (Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, Thymine, and Uracil) that carry genetic information.
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**: This primary energy-transfer molecule in cells contains nitrogen within its **adenine** moiety.
 
• **Vitamins and Alkaloids**: Many metabolic regulators and secondary metabolites also incorporate nitrogen into their chemical frameworks.
 
• **Nitrogen Cycle**: Since atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) cannot be used directly by most organisms, it must be converted into organic forms through **nitrogen fixation** by bacteria like **Rhizobium**.

questions.question: Global Trade Outlook and Statistics 2025 was published by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Trade Organization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Trade Outlook and Statistics** is a flagship annual report published by the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** that provides a comprehensive analysis of the latest developments in **world trade**.
 
• The **2025 edition** of the report offers detailed projections for **global merchandise trade growth**, analyzing how factors like **geopolitical tensions**, inflation, and monetary policies influence trade volumes across different regions.
 
• It serves as a critical analytical tool for evaluating **trade-to-GDP ratios** and understanding the shifts in **commercial services**, including digitally delivered services which have seen significant growth in recent years.
 
• The report highlights the **resilience of supply chains** and the impact of **regional trade agreements** on the overall stability of the **multilateral trading system**.
 
• By utilizing historical data and **econometric modeling**, the WTO provides policymakers with insights into **trade costs**, commodity prices, and the potential risks facing the **global economy** in the short to medium term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:

 
 
• Established: **1 January 1995**, following the **Marrakesh Agreement**.
 
• Headquarters: **Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• Role: It is the only international organization dealing with the **global rules of trade** between nations, aiming to ensure that trade flows as smoothly and freely as possible.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**:
 
 
• Primary Publication: Known for the **World Economic Outlook (WEO)** and the **Global Financial Stability Report**.
 
• Focus: Monitors the **international monetary system** and provides loans to member countries facing balance of payments problems.
 
 
 
• **World Bank**:
 
 
• Primary Publication: Publishes the **World Development Report** and **Global Economic Prospects**.
 
• Focus: Provides **financial and technical assistance** to developing countries for development projects to reduce poverty.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO**:
 
 
• Focus: Specializes in **education, science, and culture**; it publishes the **Global Education Monitoring Report**.
